text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰقَوْمِ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْأَرْضَ ٱلْمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِى كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِكُمْ فَتَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَٰسِرِينَ

words.gloss_range: vocative call particle opening direct address before the command
words.prose: {{ar:يَٰ}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens as a live call, so the command that follows is not reported from a distance. Its long vocative onset keeps the audience in direct contact before the first imperative arrives.

topics.headline: direct vocative opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah begin as live address before it becomes command.
topics.reason: The QAC row identifies a vocative particle, and the attachment evidence ties the following people-noun to the command frame.

topics.headline: address continuity and delayed command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call sustains one audience across the surrounding speech and briefly delays the first command.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows press the opening formula, sound delay, and continuity across the boundary without contradicting the local vocative parse.

words.gloss_range: possessive vocative for the addressed people; canonical form keeps speaker relation while variant evidence highlights direct address pressure
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishing, and collective peoplehood; locally the noun names the addressed community rather than an establishing action
words.prose: {{ar:قَوْمِ}} ({{tr:qawmi}}) names the audience as a possessed vocative, so the call is intimate and collective at once. The root pressure of {{ar:ق و م}} ({{tr:q-w-m}}) lets the peoplehood feel like a summons to stand into responsibility, while the canonical case keeps the local reading as address, not an independent establishing verb.

topics.headline: possessive vocative addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressed group is both directly summoned and held in relation to the speaker.
topics.reason: The canonical QAC grammar gives a genitive possessive vocative, while the variant rows are useful as contrast for address texture rather than replacements of the local form.

topics.headline: collective standing responsibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the people as one collective agent asked to stand forward into the command, not as isolated listeners.
topics.reason: The root and noun-family rows support collective peoplehood and standing pressure, and local grammar makes that collective the addressee of the commands.

topics.headline: prophetic address formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can place this call within the repeated prophetic address formula while still reading the local command scene.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete narrative and formula links, including 5:41 and broader prophetic address usage, with no conflict against the local vocative.

words.gloss_range: direct plural imperative of entry into a definite land object, making obedience a threshold-crossing act
words.root_gloss_range: entering, going inside, and domain-crossing; locally Form I imperative selects physical entry into the commanded territory
words.prose: {{ar:ٱدْخُلُوا۟}} ({{tr:udkhulū}}) converts the call into a plural imperative with an explicit object. Through the root {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}), obedience is pictured as crossing a threshold into the commanded domain, and the narrative tension is that this commanded entry will become the refusal test.

topics.headline: imperative entry into object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speech becomes an immediate plural command aimed at a definite object.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment data identify a Form I plural imperative with an explicit accusative object.

topics.headline: threshold crossing obedience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels obedience as crossing into a domain rather than merely agreeing with an instruction.
topics.reason: The root rows press boundary-crossing and the local direct object licenses concrete entry into the land.

topics.headline: entry command as narrative test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this command as the action test that the next ayah will answer by refusal.
topics.reason: The narrative rows connect this imperative with the Israelite refusal sequence, while local grammar keeps the immediate force as command.

words.gloss_range: definite accusative land as the object of entry, narrowed from earth generally to a known consecrated territory
words.root_gloss_range: earth, ground, land, and territory; locally the definite object denotes the bounded domain to be entered
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضَ}} ({{tr:al-arḍa}}) is the definite accusative object of the entry command, so the scene narrows from earth generally to a known territory. The root {{ar:أ ر ض}} ({{tr:ʾ-r-ḍ}}) keeps the promise grounded in concrete land, while the following modifiers make that land the covenantal domain whose refusal will matter later.

topics.headline: definite accusative land object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the command has a bounded known territory as its object, not earth in general.
topics.reason: The QAC row and attachments mark the land as definite, singular, accusative, and modified by the following adjective and relative clause.

topics.headline: ground becomes covenantal territory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices sanctity and promise landing on concrete terrain rather than remaining abstract favor.
topics.reason: The broader earth or ground range is narrowed locally by definiteness, object case, and the consecrating modifiers into a specific land-domain.

topics.headline: land object anticipates wandering consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can track the same land-domain from commanded entry into the later denied wandering space.
topics.reason: The rows connect this land phrase with 5:26, where the refused domain becomes the space of wandering.

words.gloss_range: definite feminine passive participle modifying the land as a made-holy or consecrated domain
words.root_gloss_range: purity, holiness, sanctification, and consecrated space; locally Form II passive participle marks the land as sanctified
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُقَدَّسَةَ}} ({{tr:al-muqaddasata}}) agrees with the land and marks it as a consecrated, made-holy domain. The root {{ar:ق د س}} ({{tr:q-d-s}}) brings purity and sanctity pressure, but the local payoff is adjectival: the object to be entered is already characterized as sanctified space.

topics.headline: concordant made-holy adjective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees holiness grammatically fastened onto the land as its present status.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment evidence mark a definite feminine accusative Form II passive participle agreeing with the land.

topics.headline: purity grounding holiness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that holiness is felt through purity and consecration, while the local form keeps it as a land adjective.
topics.reason: The q-d-s rows press purity and holiness together; local grammar narrows the payoff to the land's described consecrated status.

topics.headline: sanctified space network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the land linked with the Mūsā sanctified-space pattern, including the sanctified valley scenes at 20:12 and 79:16.
topics.reason: The supplied rows explicitly relate the consecrated land to sanctified spaces in the Mūsā narrative, including 20:12 and 79:16.

words.gloss_range: feminine relative pronoun binding the authorization clause back to the land phrase
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّتِى}} ({{tr:allatī}}) fastens the following clause back onto the land phrase. It turns the object from a described holy territory into the very territory authorized by completed decree.

topics.headline: relative clause authorization link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the land description does not stop at holiness; it immediately receives a decree-clause authorization.
topics.reason: The QAC row and attachments identify the feminine relative pronoun as modifying the land phrase and introducing the authorization clause.

topics.headline: feminine pivot and clause break
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the object phrase pivot from description into divine decree without changing referent.
topics.reason: The feminine form preserves agreement with the land while the CRITICAL rows observe the pivot from adjective to decree.

words.gloss_range: completed divine writing or prescription directed benefactively toward the addressees
words.root_gloss_range: writing, prescribing, decreeing, binding, and joining; locally the perfect verb presents a completed allotment rather than a burden imposed upon them
words.prose: {{ar:كَتَبَ}} ({{tr:kataba}}) states the authorization as a completed act. The root {{ar:ك ت ب}} ({{tr:k-t-b}}) keeps writing, prescription, and binding pressure alive, but the local beneficiary construction makes the decree face toward the people as allotted favor rather than as a burden placed upon them.

topics.headline: completed benefactive decree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entry command rests on a decree already completed for the addressees.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect Form I and takes a beneficiary phrase, so the decree grounds the command as completed allotment.

topics.headline: writing as binding act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the decree as something inscribed and binding, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as divine prescription/allotment.
topics.reason: The root rows preserve writing, prescribing, and binding pressure; local construction narrows it away from a literal act of sewing or writing material.

topics.headline: decree language network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this favorable writing contrasted with burden or prescription language elsewhere, including the contrast with 5:45.
topics.reason: The rows compare the benefactive construction here with other k-t-b constructions, especially 5:45, without overriding the local benefactive frame.

words.gloss_range: explicit nominative divine subject of the completed decree
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship-authority, and the proper divine name; locally the proper name supplies the subject and source of the land decree
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is the explicit nominative subject of the decree. The root display {{ar:أ ل ه}} ({{tr:ʾ-l-h}}) preserves the proper-name and worship-authority pressure, so the authorization is anchored in named divine authority, not in an unnamed force.

topics.headline: explicit divine subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the authority behind the land decree is named explicitly in the middle of the ayah.
topics.reason: The proper divine name is nominative and follows the verb as its explicit subject.

topics.headline: proper name and worship authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the decree as coming from the definite worship-authority, not a generic power.
topics.reason: The derivational rows carry worship-authority pressure, while the local form is a proper name functioning as subject.

topics.headline: Surah authority marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this explicit divine authority with Surah 5's wider authority and consequence field, including 5:53.
topics.reason: The rows link divine naming, writing, land, and later loss formulas in Surah 5 without altering the local subject relation.

words.gloss_range: benefactive prepositional phrase with plural suffix, identifying the addressees as recipients of the decree
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) closes the decree as benefactive: the writing is for the addressed group. The suffix keeps the same audience in view just before the ayah turns from authorization to prohibition.

topics.headline: benefactive recipient phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the written decree is directed for the addressees rather than against them.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence makes the preposition and suffix complete the decree as its beneficiary phrase.

topics.headline: suffix seals authorization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same addressed group carried from gift-memory into the command before the warning begins.
topics.reason: The plural suffix identifies the beneficiaries and closes the authorization clause before the coordinated prohibition.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that turns from positive command and authorization to the matching prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the authorization-command unit to the prohibition that follows. Its small pivot makes the positive movement into the land and the negative warning against reversal part of one coordinated address.

topics.headline: coordination from command to prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning is joined to the command as the other side of the same address.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the prohibition after the imperative clause rather than starting a detached warning.

topics.headline: positive and negative action poles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah pivot from entering forward to refusing backward movement.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows describe the conjunction as a pivot between the command to enter and the prohibition against retreat.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle setting negation scope over the following jussive verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) sets a real prohibition over the coming jussive verb. The warning chain begins here: the ayah does not merely advise against retreat but grammatically blocks it before naming the consequence.

topics.headline: prohibitive scope over jussive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the next action is not merely discouraged; it is grammatically prohibited.
topics.reason: The QAC row identifies the particle as prohibitive and the attachment support marks the following clause as a coordinated prohibition.

topics.headline: prohibition begins consequence chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the warning chain begin at the negation particle before it reaches the result clause.
topics.reason: The rows connect the prohibitive particle to the retreat verb and the later consequence clause.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form VIII prohibition against self-reversing retreat onto the body-axis complement
words.root_gloss_range: returning, repelling, restoring, and turning back; locally Form VIII makes the warned reversal self-involving rather than externally caused
words.prose: {{ar:تَرْتَدُّوا۟}} ({{tr:tartaddū}}) is the jussive verb under the prohibition, naming the live alternative to entering. The root {{ar:ر د د}} ({{tr:r-d-d}}) carries return and reversal, and Form VIII makes that reversal self-involving before the body-axis complement supplies its direction.

topics.headline: live prohibition against retreat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the forbidden act as the live alternative to entering: turning back after being commanded forward.
topics.reason: The verb is jussive after the prohibitive particle and forms the prohibited clause that triggers the result.

topics.headline: self-reversal onto body axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the retreat as a self-involving reversal aimed onto the addressees' own backward axis.
topics.reason: The Form VIII rows support reflexive reversal, and the prepositional complement supplies the local body-axis limit.

topics.headline: reversal network and consequence formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this self-reversal with the exact consequence warning echoed at 3:149.
topics.reason: The supplied rows name 3:149 as a near-exact parallel and connect the local return-root with the later overturning result.

topics.headline: geminated reversal pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the doubled consonantal pressure matching the warned reversal by the same addressed group.
topics.reason: The assimilation and sound rows are compatible with the local Form VIII morphology and reinforce the same reversal payoff.

words.gloss_range: preposition governing the backs phrase and making the reversal spatially directional
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) gives the forbidden reversal a spatial axis. It does not leave retreat abstract; it carries the verb into an embodied back-turning idiom.

topics.headline: directional axis for reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that retreat is given a spatial axis, not left as an abstract refusal.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the backs phrase and marks the surface or direction of the turning back.

topics.headline: compact idiom and delayed turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the preposition as a compact hinge that carries the verb into an embodied idiom.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows press the bound prepositional idiom and cadence before the backs noun, which fits the local governed phrase.

words.gloss_range: possessed broken plural backs, carrying both concrete rear-body image and aftermath pressure
words.root_gloss_range: back, behind, aftermath, trace, and management/planning extensions; locally the concrete plural backs image is selected while aftermath pressure remains relevant
words.prose: {{ar:أَدْبَارِكُمْ}} ({{tr:adbārikum}}) makes the retreat bodily and communal: the backs are possessed by the addressed plural group. The root {{ar:د ب ر}} ({{tr:d-b-r}}) lets the concrete rear image carry behind-and-aftermath pressure, so the warning lands on their own backward orientation before consequence is named.

topics.headline: possessed plural body image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader pictures the whole addressed community by its own backs, not as a single abstract retreat.
topics.reason: The noun is a governed broken plural with a second-person plural suffix, matching the addressed group.

topics.headline: backs and aftermath pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the body image open into aftermath: turning back also means moving into what lies behind and after.
topics.reason: The local selected sense is concrete backs, while d-b-r rows preserve behind, trace, and aftermath pressure without replacing the noun.

topics.headline: reversal parallels and planning contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the backs idiom with face-to-back reversal at 4:47 and with the planning-field contrast without making those the local sense.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give 4:47 and d-b-r management extensions; these survive as contrastive pressure while the local noun remains concrete backs.

topics.headline: back image before result connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first half of the warning lands on a vivid rear-body image before the result connector releases the consequence.
topics.reason: The word closes the prohibition phrase before the causal result clause, and the rarity/sound rows reinforce that marked landing.

words.gloss_range: causal result connector joining the forbidden retreat to its consequence
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the forbidden retreat into cause and the next clause into result. Its brevity makes the consequence feel immediate rather than loosely coordinated.

topics.headline: causal result connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that overturning is grammatically presented as the result of retreat, not a loose next event.
topics.reason: The QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as causal fa introducing the result clause.

topics.headline: immediate fused consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the consequence snap onto the preceding warning with immediate sequence and cadence.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows press both causation and quick sequence, and the proclitic attachment visibly fuses the result marker to the following verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form VII result verb: the addressees would be overturned or inverted as a consequence
words.root_gloss_range: turning, overturning, inversion, return, and heart fluctuation; locally Form VII selects undergone state reversal after retreat
words.prose: {{ar:تَنقَلِبُوا۟}} ({{tr:tanqalibū}}) is governed by the causal result frame, so the overturning depends on the forbidden retreat. The root {{ar:ق ل ب}} ({{tr:q-l-b}}) gives more than return: Form VII makes the addressees undergo inversion, and the following loss-state shows what that inversion becomes.

topics.headline: fa-governed result verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the overturning depends grammatically on the retreat clause.
topics.reason: The verb is subjunctive after causal fa and belongs to the result clause, not an independent prediction.

topics.headline: undergone overturning into loss state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the addressees undergoing a state inversion whose simultaneous condition is loss.
topics.reason: The Form VII rows support passive-reflexive or middle force, and the attachment evidence links the following participle as the circumstantial state.

topics.headline: heart and inversion pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears more than simple return: the result is a whole-state inversion with heart-turning resonance held in the background.
topics.reason: The q-l-b rows press return, inversion, and heart fluctuation; local grammar narrows the selected sense to undergone overturning in the result clause.

topics.headline: outcome formula network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can identify the exact outcome formula shared with 3:149, now applied to retreat from entry.
topics.reason: The supplied rows explicitly name the exact phrase parallel at 3:149 and connect it with Surah 5 reversal and heart fields.

topics.headline: penultimate move into final loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the penultimate verb drive the warning into its final loss label.
topics.reason: The temporal and sound rows converge with the grammar: the result verb leads directly into the final circumstantial participle.

words.gloss_range: accusative plural active participle as circumstantial loss-state during the overturning
words.root_gloss_range: loss, diminution, deficit, and failed outcome; locally the participle classifies the addressees as in a state of loss
words.prose: {{ar:خَٰسِرِينَ}} ({{tr:khāsirīn}}) is the circumstantial state in which the overturning would occur. The root {{ar:خ س ر}} ({{tr:kh-s-r}}) brings loss and diminution pressure, and the active participle makes the warning close on a settled condition: the addressees would be people characterized by loss.

topics.headline: circumstantial loss state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that loss is simultaneous with the overturning, not an extra event added afterward.
topics.reason: The active participle is accusative ḥāl agreeing with the subject of the result verb.

topics.headline: deficit becomes identity label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels loss as a measurable deficit that settles into a descriptive status.
topics.reason: The root rows preserve diminution and commercial-loss pressure, while the local participle applies it as an evaluative state label.

topics.headline: Surah and cross-formula loss field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this final label with Surah 5 failure scenes and the flip-loss relation made explicit at 22:11.
topics.reason: The supplied rows cite Surah 5 occurrences at 5:5, 5:30, and 5:53, plus 22:11 and the 3:149 formula.

topics.headline: final warning landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the whole command-prohibition sequence close on the named condition of loss.
topics.reason: The final-position and cadence rows match the grammar of the participle as the ayah's closing state label.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative to enter, the qualified land, and the clause that God wrote it for the addressees.
baseline_models.mechanism: Divine inscription establishes an assigned destination, while the imperative makes crossing into it the act that realizes the assignment. The gift is not presented as self-executing possession.

activation_trace.role: Movement into an interior supplies the realizing act by which the assignment becomes inhabited rather than merely named.
A purified-place image qualifies the destination as a bounded sacred place rather than generic territory.
Binding inscription that establishes a ruling or allotment supplies the assignment's normative force.

changed_reading.before: The ayah simply reports that a territory has been granted and orders its occupation.
changed_reading.after: The ayah presents an assigned sacred destination whose grant must be enacted by entry.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The vocative naming a people, the plural imperative, and the prohibition on turning back.
baseline_models.mechanism: The address names an existing collectivity, but the rising-and-resolve branch makes its collective identity active: they become this people by rising together to the assigned act. Recurrent hesitation and mutual back-turning threaten to dissolve that posture.

activation_trace.role: The human-group image supplies the explicit collective being addressed.
Rising with resolve activates a performative dimension in that collective name: the group must stand up to its task.
Repetition, oscillation, and hesitation make the forbidden reversal a failure to sustain common resolve.
People turning their backs on one another supplies the social fracture latent in a plural retreat.

changed_reading.before: A pre-existing people receives a collective travel or battle order.
changed_reading.after: The order tests whether the addressees can constitute themselves as a people that rises and holds together in action.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence of returning, backs, turning over, and becoming losers.
baseline_models.mechanism: Three successive orientation roots turn retreat into a process rather than a single step: return takes the body backward, backward orientation flips the course, and the flip produces a diminished state. Loss is grammatically downstream of self-reversal.

activation_trace.role: Return to a prior place or state initiates the reversal sequence.
The back side gives the return a concrete bodily and directional orientation.
Turning a thing from one face to another converts backward motion into a changed condition.
General diminishment names the terminal state generated by the reversal.

changed_reading.before: Loss is an external penalty imposed after disobedient retreat.
changed_reading.after: Retreat is itself an inversion process that converts the agents into a diminished outcome.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet's opening demand for complete fulfillment of bound obligations and its later recalled covenant revise divine writing from a deed of effortless possession into a commission whose human side is fulfilled by entry.

activation_trace.role: Binding inscription supplies the focus assignment that the covenant frame can construe as obligatory.
Actual passage inward supplies the performance by which the written commission is answered.
Completion without deficiency makes covenant response a fully performed act rather than verbal assent.
A firmly bound obligation supplies the legal-social frame for the focus assignment.
The emphatic covenant image joins remembered divine favor to an already confirmed human commitment.

structural_cues: 5:1 opens the packet by coupling faith with fulfillment of contracts.
5:7 recalls a covenant in the same sequence as hearing and obeying, and 5:12 again couples covenantal acts with promised entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies binding, fulfillment, and covenant language; I apply that frame to the focus inscription and infer that entry is its required performance. The live alternative is that the writing denotes an unconditional grant with obedience only added afterward.

changed_reading.before: God's writing is primarily a title to a promised place.
changed_reading.after: God's writing is also a covenantal commission: the allotted gift and the obligation to enter are one transaction.

context_deltas.mechanism: Purification elsewhere in the packet is something performed and produced, while sustained standing, equity, and just conduct define a communal vocation. These cues activate the sacred quality of the land as an order the entrants must embody and maintain, not only a property the location already has.

activation_trace.role: Purity and removal from defilement supply the focus quality that can be enacted as well as located.
An inward or interior dimension lets entry describe incorporation into an order, while remaining anchored in the spatial imperative.
Purification through washing supplies a practiced transition from an unready state to a prepared one.
Sustained guardianship places standing responsibility beside the naming of a people and gives holiness a communal bearer.
Equity supplies the public norm the standing collective is charged to preserve.
Justice in conduct turns the sacred order into an enacted social practice.

structural_cues: 5:6 moves from bodily purification to God's stated purpose of purifying the addressees.
5:8 commands an enduring stance for God as witnesses with equity even toward a hated people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies produced purification and a justice-bearing collective; I infer that entrants are to reproduce those qualities in the sacred land. The live alternative is that the land's holiness is wholly locative and does not describe its entrants.

changed_reading.before: The command is to occupy a place that is already holy.
changed_reading.after: The command is also to enter and sustain a purified, just communal order appropriate to that place.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding recollection of favor and sovereignty supplies prior capacity, while the next objection supplies real coercive opposition. The written land therefore reads less like entitlement to frictionless possession and more like responsibility proportionate to an already given capacity.

activation_trace.role: The binding allotment supplies the responsibility whose feasibility is tested by the surrounding claims of capacity and opposition.
A bestowed good condition supplies remembered enablement before the command is issued.
Sovereignty and authority supply political capacity rather than merely a claim to property.
Coercive overpowering names the contrary force that makes exercise of the prior capacity costly.

structural_cues: 5:20 lists divine favors and the making of kings immediately before the focus command.
5:22 answers the command by naming the inhabitants' overpowering force.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prior favor, sovereignty, and opposing coercion; I infer that the recollection establishes capacity for responsibility rather than a guarantee of ease. The live alternative is that 5:20 is encouragement by status alone.

changed_reading.before: Being written the land means the recipients are entitled to possess it without remainder.
changed_reading.after: Being written the land assigns empowered recipients a responsibility whose reality is shown precisely by resistance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The response to the focus imperative exposes two rival causal programs. The refusers require the obstacle to exit before they enter; the two men require entry through the gate before victory, with reliance sustaining the passage. Entry changes from arrival after safety into the threshold act through which conditions can change.

activation_trace.role: The focus command to move inward supplies the disputed first action in both causal programs.
Repeated inward movement is postponed and made conditional, exposing the refusers' sequence.
Movement outward names the prerequisite the refusers demand before undertaking entry.
Repeated inward movement is instead placed before the predicted change in power.
The entrance of a thing gives the command a concrete threshold at which commitment precedes outcome.
Overcoming force is placed after gate-entry, making victory the predicted consequence rather than its prerequisite.
Reliant dependence supplies the stance that can sustain action before control of the result.

structural_cues: 5:22 uses an until-condition: they will enter only after the inhabitants leave.
5:23 reverses that order: enter the gate, then overcoming follows.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the two conditional sequences; I read their ordering as rival causal models and treat gate-entry as condition-changing action. The live alternative is that 5:23 offers encouragement specific to this battle, not a general threshold mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Enter once the destination is secure enough to receive you.
changed_reading.after: Enter the exposed threshold first; committed passage, not prior control, is the action through which the promised outcome becomes possible.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier sustained standing for God activates the rising potential in the focus address. The later declaration of sitting out the action, followed by a request for separation, then shows collective identity changing with posture: refusal does not leave the people socially unchanged.

activation_trace.role: The explicit human collective supplies the identity placed under pressure by the command.
Rising with resolve supplies the active posture latent in the collective address.
Sustained guardianship places responsible standing beside the naming of a people and prepares the focus vocative as a vocation.
Sitting out an action supplies the explicit counter-posture to collective rising.
Distinguishing and separating supplies the social consequence of the opposed postures.

structural_cues: 5:8 commands sustained standing for God before the narrative names the focus addressees as a people.
5:24 ends the refusal with a declaration of sitting, and 5:25 immediately asks for separation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies standing language, a sitting refusal, and a separation request; I connect them as a social mechanism in the focus collective noun. The live alternative is a rhetorical contrast that does not redefine group membership.

changed_reading.before: The vocative addresses a stable people who may either obey or disobey.
changed_reading.after: The vocative calls a people into being through responsible rising; choosing to sit fractures the very collectivity being addressed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The aftermath externalizes the focus reversal. Declared sitting does not preserve a safe stationary outside; prohibition, measured years, and wandering on the same land-root convert a bounded sacred destination into prolonged unarrival. The loss is orientation and time as well as territory.

activation_trace.role: Ground opposite the sky supplies the concrete spatial field first presented as a destination.
The purified place gives that field bounded destination-quality.
Turning from one face to another supplies the spatial conversion later displayed by wandering.
Diminishment receives temporal and spatial content from the aftermath.
Fixed sitting supplies the attempted stationary alternative to risky entry.
Prevention and prohibition reverse access to the place previously written for them.
The year image makes lost orientation a measured duration rather than an instantaneous setback.
The same ground image returns as the medium of wandering instead of the reached destination.

structural_cues: The attempted alternative in 5:24 is to remain seated here.
In 5:26 the land is barred for forty years and becomes the field of wandering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the refusal, prohibition, duration, and wandering; I apply that consequence back to the focus turning and loss verbs and infer a conversion from destination to unarrival. The live alternative is to treat 5:26 only as an externally imposed penalty.

changed_reading.before: Turning back means missing the destination or returning to a prior place.
changed_reading.after: Turning back converts destination into circulation: the same land remains underfoot, but no longer functions as arrival, and years become part of the loss.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it joins a ship branch of the sacredness root to a boat-pole branch under the alternate mapping of the return root. Both remain tied to focus words and produce a coherent directional mechanism, but downstream prose should present it only as a cross-domain material analogy, never as a lexical claim that the sacred land is a ship.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The qualified destination, the prohibition on reversal, and the resulting destination or outcome.

activation_trace.role: A great-vessel image gives the sacred destination an exploratory container of passage.
Pushing a vessel with a pole supplies sustained directional effort as the material opposite of reversal.
Movement toward an outcome supplies the navigational destination threatened by a change of course.

changed_reading.before: The ayah gives a literal land-entry command and warns against retreat.
changed_reading.after: As a material analogy, it depicts committed passage that must keep its propulsion and heading or lose its destination.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links registration, an alternate stripping branch, separation, and a fruit leaving its shell. The chain remains anchored in the focus inscription, reversal, and loss and is sharpened by 5:25, but it should be rendered as an exploratory social-material model of de-enrollment, not as the lexical meaning of either reversal or transgression.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: God's writing for the group, the forbidden reversal, and becoming diminished.

activation_trace.role: Entering a name in a register or cohort supplies an enrollment image for the written assignment.
Stripping away a covering supplies the material image of exposing oneself by reversal.
Diminishment names the resulting loss of protected or enrolled standing.
Explicit distinction and separation supplies the social result of opposed responses.
A ripe fruit leaving its shell makes separation from a containing order materially visible.

changed_reading.before: Retreat forfeits access to an assigned possession.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, retreat strips the refusers out of the divinely inscribed cohort, so territorial loss is also loss of enrolled standing.

strongest_changes: The covenant roots turn what is written for the group from a passive deed into a commission fulfilled through entry.
The rival sequences in 5:22-23 make gate-entry a condition-changing act rather than arrival after safety.
Standing, sitting, and separation make the command constitutive of collective identity.
The aftermath converts sacred destination into measured wandering, giving loss spatial and temporal form.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah already contains a dense reversal cascade, and the packet externalizes each stage as covenant, threshold, posture, separation, prohibition, and wandering. The alternate mapping of the return root also supported two contained material outliers without displacing the stronger readings.
remaining_uncertainties: The purity-and-justice model may describe what entrants must embody, or the sacred adjective may remain only locative.
The standing potential in the collective noun is structurally reinforced but still depends on cross-form activation.
The alternate mapped-root outliers should remain analogical and exploratory.
Divine writing may retain an unconditional gift sense alongside the covenantal commission.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Entry opposes a double backward turn.** `ر د د B001` is returning, `د ب ر B003` turning the back, and `ق ل ب B004` reversal. The command to enter is followed by three backward images. I infer that loss (`خ س ر B001`, deficiency) is generated by recursive retreat, not merely failure to acquire territory.
2. **Holiness is a prepared place of purification.** `ق د س B002` supplies a purified sacred place. Because the land is also “written” for them, I infer that entry is meant to realize a prescribed purifying relation; possession without responsive entry remains unrealized inscription.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The command establishes a directional test.** Fixed **ر د د / B001** (“returning or sending back”) and **د ب ر / B001** (“the rear or back of a thing”) turn *lā tartaddū ʿalā adbārikum* into a bodily reversal opposite *udkhulū*. The next three ayat repeatedly suspend entry, while 5:26 replaces purposeful advance with wandering. I infer that loss occurs when agents rotate the capacity bestowed in 5:20 away from its assigned object. The ayah reads as a test of maintained forward orientation, not merely a prohibition on geographical retreat.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:26 supplied the strongest later activation: turning back does not preserve rest but converts directed entry into trackless motion.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, sözcüğün temel olarak kadınlar dışındaki erkekler topluluğunu anlattığını, kadınların ancak ikincil biçimde kapsama girebildiğini ve insan dışı varlıklara aktarılabildiğini gösterir. identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir varlığın üzerindeki doğal örtünün bulunmaması veya giderilmesi ortaklığını açıkça destekler. Ancak dal için yapraksızlık ile kabuğun soyulması birlikte aktarılırken bir kaynak dalı bu sıfatla nitelemeyi reddeder; bu nedenle dal örneği genel çekirdeğin tartışmasız bir uygulaması olarak sunulmamalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel örtüsüzlük veya örtüyü giderme çekirdeğini verir; yapraksız dal, sakalsız genç, tüysüz at ve bitkisiz arazi okumaları yalnız kendi ad öbeklerine bağlı uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin üzerinde doğal olarak bulunan saç, kıl, tüy, yaprak, kabuk veya bitki örtüsünün hiç bulunmaması ya da üzerinden giderilmesidir. İnsan, hayvan, bitki ve araziye göre yok olan örtünün türü değişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın üstünü doğal olarak kaplayan unsurun bulunmaması veya giderilmesi anlamın ortak çekirdeğidir.
İnsan ve at gibi canlılarda sakalın, kılın veya belirli bir bölgedeki tüyün bulunmamasını anlatır.
Ağaç ve dal bağlamında yaprak ya da kabuk gibi üzerini örten unsurun yokluğunu veya giderilmesini anlatır.
Kumluk ve arazi bağlamında bitki yetişmemesini ve yüzeyin bitki örtüsünden yoksun kalmasını anlatır.
Dalın bu sıfatla nitelenmesi kaynaklarda aynı ölçüde kabul edilmez; bu kullanım ihtiyatla değerlendirilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak alanı saç, kıl, yaprak, kabuk veya bitki gibi doğal bir örtünün yokluğudur. Dalın adlandırılmasında bir kabul ayrılığı bulunsa da ağaç, genç, at ve bitkisiz kumluk örnekleri bu ortak alanı somutlaştırır.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlamları arka taraf ve son nokta çevresinden sırt çevirme, sonuca bakarak planlama, iz bırakmadan yok etme ve çok sayıda özel nesne ya da teknik adına yayılır. Rüzgâr, gök cismi, böcek topluluğu, tarla bölmesi, yara, oyun oku ve güreş tutuşu gibi dallar bu genişlemenin yerleşmiş özel alanlarıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir nesneyi yüzünden ya da yönünden başka yöne çevirmeyi, altüst etmeyi, bir kişiyi istediği yönden saptırmayı ve işleri düşünerek evirip çevirmeyi aynı dönüştürme çekirdeğine bağlar. Tamlama bağlı kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin özel uygulamalarıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın çevirme çekirdeğini, kişi saptırma ve işleri düşünme gibi tamlama bağlı kullanımlardan ayrı gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bulunduğu yüzden veya yönden başka yüze, başka yöne ya da ters duruma çevirmek; kişiyi hedeflediği yönden saptırmak ve işleri zihinde evirip çevirerek değerlendirmek anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi yüzünden başka yüze çevirmek, ters çevirmek veya altüst etmektir.

İşleri yönetmek ve üzerinde düşünüp taşınmak için zihinde evirip çevirmek de bu alana bağlıdır.
Ekmek, göz, toprak aleti, renk sapması ve satın alınan kişiyi inceleme gibi özel örnekler aynı çevirmeye dayanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, yön ya da yüz değiştirme çekirdeğini verir; kişi saptırma, işleri düşünme ve somut örnekler bu çekirdeğin özel kullanımlarıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak cümlesi, dalın ortak çekirdeğini bir şeyin önceki miktarından, bütünlüğünden veya değerinden eksilmesi olarak kurar. Tartı örneği bu genel çekirdeğin bir gerçekleşmesidir; alım satım, ölçüde eksik verme ve yıkıma uğrama ise ayrı dallarda özelleşir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik sınıf çıplaktır; tanım, herhangi bir özel söz dizimine bağlı olmadan genel eksilme çekirdeğini verir ve öteki dalların bağlama özgü anlamlarını içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin miktarından, bütünlüğünden veya değerinden bir bölümün gitmesi ve böylece önceki düzeyinin altına düşmesidir.

facets.statement: Bir şey, sahip olduğu miktarın, bütünlüğün veya değerin bir bölümünü yitirir.
Eksilme tartıda görülebilir, ancak dalın kapsamı tartıyla sınırlı değildir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği, bir şeyin miktar veya değer bakımından eksilmesidir; tek asıl açıklaması Maqayis'e, tartıda veya başka şeyde eksilme ayrıntısı ise Tahdhib'e aittir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir varlığın miktar, bütünlük veya değer bakımından önceki düzeyinin altına düşmesini alan belirtmeden anlatırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Genel azalma ile değer veya bütünlük yitimini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Miktarı gözlenebilen bir şeyin önceki düzeyinin altına inmesini akıcı biçimde anlatan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Önceki miktarın altına düşme yönünü açıkça korur.
error_profile.loses: Bütünlük veya değer kaybı biçimindeki daha geniş uygulamayı belirtmez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir sonuç ya da elde kalan miktar beklenen düzeye ulaşmadığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Beklenen veya önceki düzeyin altında kalma sonucunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Eksilmeye yol açan süreci ve genel değer yitimini açıkça taşımaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: eksilme ya da eksik kalan sonuç

error_profile.preserves: Olumsuz bir sonuç ve yitim duygusunu kısmen korur.
error_profile.loses: Miktar, bütünlük veya değerdeki yalın eksilmeyi karşılamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, eksilmeyi aynı zamanda değer veya bütünlük yitimi olarak çerçeveler.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, artışın karşıtı olan nicel azalmayı geçişli ve geçişsiz kullanımlarıyla daha nötr biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: değer yitimi ile nötr nicel azalma
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyin önceki miktarından bir bölümün gitmesini ve daha az hale gelmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal genel ve nötr bir azalma sözlüğü sunarken odak dal, eksilmeyi bir şeyden pay veya değer gitmesi yönüyle öne çıkarır; bu yüzden kapsamlar güçlü biçimde örtüşse de her bağlamda birbirinin yerine geçmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, alan belirtmeden her türlü miktar veya değer eksilmesini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, alım satımda kazanç doğmamasını veya anaparanın eksilmesini şart koşar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da eldeki değerin azalması ortak bir sonuç olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ticari dalın çekirdeğinde alım satım ve kazanç beklentisi vardır; odak dalda ise böyle bir işlem veya beklenti bulunması gerekmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, eksilmenin kendisini anlatır ve bir ölçme işlemi gerektirmez.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, bir failin ölçü veya tartı sonucunu eksik bırakmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da ortaya çıkan sonuç beklenen miktardan daha azdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal durum veya sonuç düzeyinde genel eksilmeyi karşılar; komşu dal ise ölçme ya da tartma sırasında nesneyi eksik bırakmaya bağlı geçişli bir işlemdir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; genel nicel azalma ve iki kardeş özelleşme sınırı en çok açıklayan karşıtlıklar olarak seçildi. Öteki adaylar aynı eksilme alanındaki daha dar örnekleri yineliyor veya yalnızca uzak bir ölçme ve yokluk alanını paylaşıyor.
